basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A provider-client view of services and assets, not a CMDB or asset master.
Records which system masters each fact and routes changes there.
Keeps desired and observed state apart.
Enforces client isolation in a multi-tenant provider context.

may: Register a graph for a client within declared policy.
Route proposed changes to the owning master system.
Build projections allowed for a given role and purpose.
Reconcile observed state with desired state and report drift.
mustNot: Access or mix data across clients.
Retry a non-idempotent change after a timeout without reconciling.
Change facts whose owner or identity is unresolved.
Treat the graph as proof of client acceptance or ownership.

considerations: Clients entrust providers with access to critical systems; isolation failures can expose many organizations.
Outages caused by wrong changes affect people who depend on client services.
Provider lock-in through incomplete handover harms clients.

items: A service graph has a client tenant, provider, service and asset nodes, dependencies and per-fact master references.
Confused with a CMDB, a monitoring topology and an asset inventory.
Duplicate or conflicting changes after timeouts.
